conventions.convention: Signature is (-,+,+,+). The curved background is a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold; its metric and time orientation are fixed, and no field equation or completeness hypothesis is included.

Massive worldlines are C² curves on open real intervals with future timelike tangent. Null worldlines have nonzero future null tangent. A pointwise observer has g(n,n)=-1; observers, congruences, tetrads and charts are distinct objects.
SI inertial coordinates are x⁰=ct and spatial coordinates in metres; c is in metres per second and proper time in seconds.
The clock postulate permits continuous piecewise-C¹ future timelike paths with a finite partition and timelike one-sided endpoint tangents; clock increments are summed across corners.

Massive stationarity uses finite segments and fixed-endpoint C² variations through future timelike curves. C¹ increasing diffeomorphisms preserve the length integral; C² diffeomorphisms preserve the stated curve and variation class.

The null action uses a smooth positive einbein, unrestricted causal character for the varied curves, independent fixed-endpoint C² curve variations and smooth interior einbein variations. Physical null tangents are nonzero and future-directed; P=T/e has independent initial scale and no proper-time normalization.
Massive mechanical momentum is P=mU with g(U,U)=-c². Observer quantities are q_n(P)=P+g(P,n)n and E_n(P)=-c g(P,n).

The named constant-mass force map is smooth on an open neighborhood of the future normalized timelike shell and satisfies g(V,f(p,V))=0 throughout that domain. The adopted equation is DτP=f(x,U); this is an optional interaction model.

load_bearing.statement: Fixes the prescribed flat or curved background, signature, C² future timelike and nonzero future-null worldlines, pointwise unit observers, distinct congruence/chart/tetrad meanings, and SI coordinates.

For the stated C² future timelike finite segment and fixed-endpoint C² timelike variation, δS=-mc∫g(J,D_s(T/ℓ))ds. Stationarity under all such variations is equivalent to D_s(T/ℓ)=0, equivalently DτU=0. Length is invariant under the stated increasing C¹ changes of variable, with C² required to preserve the configuration class.

For S_e=½∫(e⁻¹g(T,T)-em²c²)ds with the stated positive smooth einbein and independent variations, the stationary equations are g(T,T)+e²m²c²=0 and D_s(T/e)=0. On the massive future timelike branch e=ℓ/(mc) and T/e=mU; on the nonzero future-null branch P=T/e and dλ=e ds give dx/dλ=P and DλP=0.

A smooth force orthogonal to velocity throughout an open future-timelike velocity domain gives a unique local position/tangent solution through each normalized initial datum, smooth local dependence on initial data and smooth finite-dimensional force parameters, preservation of the future normalized timelike shell, and a unique maximal open-interval solution without a global-lifetime assertion.

For a C² future timelike curve on a nonempty open interval, τ'=ℓ/c>0, τ is an increasing C² coordinate on its open image, and U=dx/dτ=cT/ℓ satisfies g(U,U)=-c². This alone makes no physical clock identification.

In the separately adopted massive and null sectors, mechanical momentum is respectively mU or the independently scaled nonzero future-null P. For a unit future observer, q_n(P)=P+g(P,n)n and E_n(P)=-c g(P,n).

Stationary massive finite segments satisfy DτU=0 with P=mU; stationary nonzero future-null einbein segments satisfy DλP=0 with dx/dλ=P. The stated normalized massive and nonzero future-null initial data determine unique local and maximal open-interval solutions, without completeness.

concerns.concern: F3 records only that pairing a future timelike vector with an observer is strictly negative. Step 1.2 then uses positivity for null P: 'and positivity selects E_n=c√g(q,q)'. The opened supplier lem-gr-observer-pairing-with-future-causal-vectors, clause 1, does cover every nonzero future causal vector, so the deduction is valid after explicitly invoking that broader clause; the recorded fact is narrower than this proof use.
